what: Equinix owns data centres and rents space in them. Its value is not the building but the interconnection: inside its sites, thousands of networks, clouds and companies plug directly into each other.
customers: Cloud providers, telecom carriers, financial firms and enterprises renting cabinets, power and cross-connects.
money: rent for space and power, plus fees for direct connections between customers
large-scale capacity built for hyperscale cloud customers, often in joint ventures
moat: Network effects inside the building: each new network that connects makes the site more valuable to everyone else, and customers rarely unplug.
risks: Building data centres consumes enormous capital, and debt stands near $24 billion
Power availability now limits where new capacity can be added
Hyperscale cloud customers build their own sites for the largest workloads
Higher interest rates raise financing costs for a capital-hungry model
opportunities: AI workloads increase demand for interconnection between clouds and private infrastructure
Pricing power on renewals because moving racks out is costly and risky
Joint ventures let it grow hyperscale capacity without carrying all the capital
watch: Cabinet utilisation, cross-connect counts and growth in adjusted funds from operations per share.
